fields.Brand Customer Promise: A restful, consistent midscale stay with nature-inspired design, wellness-focused conveniences, and efficient spaces that keep operations simple for owners and welcoming for guests.
fields.Brand Value Proposition:
Guests: Lifestyle experience at midscale pricing—modern design, wellness conveniences, and soothing regional palettes for a restful night and repeat visits.

Owners: Among the midscale category’s lowest cost to build with a flexible prototype, durable materials, and operational efficiencies from smart layout and back-of-house design.

Choice: National and local marketing, third-party distribution relationships, qualified vendors, and cloud-based property and reservation systems.
fields.Brand Pillars:
Scenic Dreams design — nature-inspired murals, palettes (Dusk, Dawn, Twilight, Starry Night), and a recognizable purple tower exterior.

Operational efficiency — flexible small-site prototype, durable guestroom materials, efficient elevators, storage, and laundry placement.

Wellness and convenience — fitness with stretching area and refill stations; Dream Corner marketplace revenue in lobby.

Midscale value — style and efficiency balanced for developers who bet on themselves with Choice.
fields.Brand History: Sleep Inn continues Choice Hotels’ midscale legacy with the Scenic Dreams prototype—developed with developer input to deliver a cost-effective building with high guest satisfaction potential and contemporary, high-visibility design.
fields.Guest Psychographics Description: Travelers attracted to vibrant, contemporary exteriors and open, welcoming lobbies who want nature-inspired calm in the room, practical amenities (USB, smart thermostats, efficient baths), and optional indulgences from an in-lobby marketplace.
fields.Key Brand Differentiators:
Purple tower and modern wood-accent exterior with outdoor gathering and fire pit.

Eight nature-inspired lobby mural options and signature welcome wall.

Four soothing regional color palettes and durable, easy-turn guestrooms.

Prototype research cited lift in likelihood to stay and willingness to pay after exposure to design (individual results may vary).
